name: Evan Maciel
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember delivering a prescription written under a childhood name.” Saturday often includes a stop at Breakwater Way, where Evan stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I want the daughter to have somewhere safe to live after her breakup. I also deliver the tenant's medicine every week.
appearance: Evan is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a sand-colored linen shirt with a replacement button a shade darker than the others, Evan turns fully toward the person speaking when listening.
personality: Evan loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To support the daughter and the older patient's continuing care.
family: Kai Valdez is Evan’s older cousin. Evan gets to change the plan. Kai offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Reading the payslip*, Kai says, “I run a business. I came in pretending to be a worker because my own slips embarrass me.”
connections: Stella Rizzo. Identifying trees that can move helps the relative delivering medicine find a useful part in the negotiation.

reactions.situation: An elderly gardener wants to move just one tree
reactions.response: Evan checks that the tree can survive the move before it is lifted.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Evan offers to walk to the next staffed place together, at the stranger's pace, to ask about another ride.

reactions.situation: If a stranger asks to hear a private story
reactions.response: Evan offers one about their own embarrassment instead.
